page.layout: One column of running text, with the running head "PRÆFATIO" above it. Below the last line, at the right, is a small reference mark with a "5" (a foot-level note, not a catchword). No margin notes, page number, catchword or signature.

main_text.p: Liberium, Silverium, Johannem; sed malè; quia causa in his nulla erat exilii; non quia in Imperatori-bus nulla esset auctoritas.

p.i: Ita Chamierus. Hæ sunt qua-tuor maximæ, ad quas, qui non attendit, facilè omnia sursum deorsum vertet, Ecclesiam & Rcmp.[?] turbabit, Religionem destruet, cædibus et sanguine, quantum in se est, omnia replebit: qui autem eas observabit, prudenter aget magno cum bono Ecclesiæ & Reip. Possent au-tem eæ maximæ latissime dedu-ci; sed ad hypothesin descendere

page.notes: The running head reads "PRÆFATIC." in the scan; the final letter is probably O, marked [?]. "Rcmp." is read as an abbreviation of Rempub.; the first letters are uncertain. The mark below the text (§ with a faint "?" and "5") is doubtful. The paragraph division is uncertain: I took "Ita Chamierus." to begin a new line after "auctoritas.", as it does in the scan, but it may run on. The line "Liberium ..." starts mid-sentence, so cont="true" is set. The word "Johannem" is printed with a capital J, which I have kept as the consonant j. Words with a printed line-end hyphen keep it.
